analysis.evidence: The verb takes עֶרֶב ‘evening’ as its subject. The parallel וַיְהִי בֹקֶר ‘and morning came’ confirms that the first clause recounts the arrival of evening.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־.

analysis.evidence: The repeated וַיְהִי pairs עֶרֶב with בֹקֶר, “morning,” in the refrain that closes the fourth day.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The marked וַיְהִי has בֹקֶר ‘morning’ as its subject. The parallel clauses וַיְהִי עֶרֶב וַיְהִי בֹקֶר recount the arrival of evening and then morning on the fourth day.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed conjunction וַ־

analysis.evidence: וַיְהִי בֹקֶר, “and there was morning,” parallels וַיְהִי עֶרֶב, “and there was evening.” The pair marks the fourth day.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In יוֹם רְבִיעִי, the ordinal רְבִיעִי ‘fourth’ identifies the day just described by evening and morning as the fourth in the sequence.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In יוֹם רְבִיעִי, רְבִיעִי agrees with the masculine singular noun יוֹם and identifies the day as fourth in the creation sequence.
analysis.morphology: Ordinal adjective, masculine singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix.
